Adaptive: width decides, not the device
A stack of objects and a page address
What counts as the source of truth
The same demo answers with three different strings on desktop, in a browser and on Android. The compiler did the substitution - there is no runtime check for «where are we» anywhere in the app.
Close the app and open it again - the value stays. On the web the same survives a tab reload.
One resource in the source, different ones in the build. On desktop and Android it is already inside the binary; on the web it has to be downloaded, and the first frame can beat it.
Counting frames until the string shows up…
Switch the system language - both the string and the formatting change with no rebuild.
Resize the window. The number on top is the available width reported by BoxWithConstraints; the layout flips at 840 dp.
Decide by target instead of width
«It is desktop, so it is wide» - and a narrow window breaks the layout

On the left is the Navigation 3 stack - a list of objects with fields. On the right is an address string assembled from it by hand. Nothing but fifteen lines of code sits in between: the library has no route graph at all.
The stack is a plain list of objects:
The address would be %1$s (this target has no address bar)
go_router is the other way round: the stack IS a list of path strings, so the address bar works on its own - but the screen has no typed argument. That is a difference of models, not of convenience.
Favorites go into local storage. The switch changes WHAT exactly goes there: ids only, or ids together with names. While the network is up you cannot tell the difference.
